title: Cloudinary
content:
## Overview

Cloudinary is a cloud-based media management platform that provides image and video upload, storage, manipulation, optimization, and delivery via a global CDN. Integrating Cloudinary with your Emergent app enables you to offload media hosting, automatically optimize images for different devices, and apply transformations on-the-fly.

This guide walks you through connecting Cloudinary to your Emergent workspace and using it in your application.

---

## Prerequisites

Before you begin, you'll need:

- An Emergent workspace with an active app
- A Cloudinary account ([sign up free](https://cloudinary.com/users/register_free) if you don't have one)
- Your Cloudinary **Cloud Name**, **API Key**, and **API Secret** (found in the Cloudinary dashboard under **Settings → Account**)

---

## Adding Cloudinary credentials to Emergent

<Steps>
<Step title="Open your workspace settings">
Navigate to your workspace in Emergent and open **Settings** from the left sidebar.
</Step>

<Step title="Go to the Integrations tab">
Select the **Integrations** tab, then locate **Cloudinary** in the media & productivity section.
</Step>

<Step title="Enter your Cloudinary credentials">
Paste your **Cloud Name**, **API Key**, and **API Secret** into the respective fields. These values are available in your Cloudinary dashboard under **Settings → Account → API Keys**.

<Tip>
Store these credentials securely. Emergent encrypts integration secrets at rest and in transit.
</Tip>
</Step>

<Step title="Save the integration">
Click **Save**. Emergent will validate the credentials and confirm the connection.
</Step>
</Steps>

---

## Using Cloudinary in your app

Once connected, you can reference Cloudinary in chat to build features like image uploads, galleries, and on-the-fly transformations.

### Example prompts

<AccordionGroup>
<Accordion title="Upload profile pictures to Cloudinary">
"Add a profile picture upload on the user settings page. Store the images in Cloudinary and save the public URL in the user's MongoDB record."

Emergent will generate an upload widget or file input, upload to Cloudinary via its SDK, and persist the returned `secure_url` in your [database](/database-mongodb).
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Optimize and resize images automatically">
"When displaying product images, serve them from Cloudinary with automatic format selection and a max width of 800px."

The agent will construct Cloudinary transformation URLs (e.g., `w_800,f_auto,q_auto`) to deliver optimized images.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Build a photo gallery with lazy loading">
"Create a gallery page that fetches image URLs from MongoDB and displays them using Cloudinary's responsive breakpoints."

The agent will implement lazy-loaded thumbnails and full-size lightbox views, leveraging Cloudinary's transformation API.
</Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

---

## Common transformations

Cloudinary supports URL-based transformations. You can specify these in your prompts or manually in your code:

| Transformation | Parameter | Example |
|----------------|-----------|---------|
| Resize width | `w_<pixels>` | `w_400` |
| Resize height | `h_<pixels>` | `h_300` |
| Crop mode | `c_<mode>` | `c_fill`, `c_thumb` |
| Auto format | `f_auto` | Delivers WebP/AVIF where supported |
| Auto quality | `q_auto` | Optimizes compression |
| Blur | `e_blur:<strength>` | `e_blur:300` |
| Grayscale | `e_grayscale` | Converts to black-and-white |

Combine transformations in a single URL:

```
https://res.cloudinary.com/<cloud_name>/image/upload/w_600,h_400,c_fill,f_auto,q_auto/sample.jpg
```

<Info>
Ask the agent to apply specific transformations by describing the desired effect (e.g., "crop to square and optimize for mobile").
</Info>

---

## File upload patterns

Cloudinary offers several upload methods. Emergent agents can implement any of these based on your requirements:

<Columns cols={2}>
<Card title="Direct upload from browser" icon="upload">
Use Cloudinary's unsigned or signed upload presets to upload files directly from the client, bypassing your backend.
</Card>

<Card title="Server-side upload" icon="server">
Upload files via your backend (e.g., Node.js). Useful when you need to validate, resize, or process images before storing.
</Card>
</Columns>

### Unsigned vs. signed uploads

- **Unsigned**: Faster to set up; requires an upload preset configured in your Cloudinary dashboard. Best for public, low-risk uploads.
- **Signed**: Requires a signature generated server-side using your API secret. Recommended for user-generated content where you want access control.

<Warning>
Never expose your **API Secret** in client-side code. Use signed uploads or server-side proxies for secure workflows.
</Warning>

---

## Managing media assets

Cloudinary organizes assets into folders and supports tagging, metadata, and search:

- **Folders**: Specify a folder in the upload (e.g., `folder: "avatars"`). Assets are accessible at `.../<cloud_name>/image/upload/avatars/<public_id>`.
- **Tags**: Add tags during upload for easier filtering and retrieval.
- **Search & Admin API**: Use Cloudinary's Admin API to list, update, or delete assets programmatically.

You can ask Emergent agents to implement admin panels that list, search, or delete images via the Cloudinary Admin API.

---

## Video uploads and transformations

Cloudinary supports video as well as images. Common video transformations include:

- Transcoding to multiple formats (`f_auto` for adaptive delivery)
- Generating thumbnails at specific timestamps (`so_<seconds>`)
- Applying overlays, watermarks, and effects

Example prompt:

> "Let users upload demo videos to Cloudinary and display them with a play button thumbnail on the landing page."

The agent will handle upload, generate a poster image, and embed the video player.

---

## Troubleshooting

<AccordionGroup>
<Accordion title="Upload fails with 'Invalid signature'">
Check that your **API Secret** is correct and that the signature generation logic (if using signed uploads) matches Cloudinary's specification. Ensure the timestamp is recent (signatures expire after a short window).
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Images not loading or returning 404">
Verify the **Cloud Name** in your URLs. Ensure the `public_id` is correct and that the asset exists in your Cloudinary media library. Check folder paths if you're organizing assets.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Transformations not applying">
Confirm transformation syntax (e.g., `w_400,h_300,c_fill`). Transformations must appear before the `upload` segment in the URL. Clear browser cache if testing changes.
</Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

<Tip>
Use Cloudinary's [URL Inspector](https://cloudinary.com/documentation/image_transformations#url_based_image_transformations) to debug transformation URLs and preview results.
</Tip>

---

## Next steps

With Cloudinary integrated, you can now:

- Build rich media galleries and portfolios
- Implement profile picture uploads with automatic cropping
- Deliver responsive, optimized images across devices
- Add video hosting and playback features

Describe your media workflow in chat, and the Emergent agents will scaffold the upload, transformation, and display logic for you.
